$comment: The macOS 27 light-standard material, as a PATCH over the unmoved runtime
default — W29 Decision Log 1 (i). It is not the identity with that default and
carries no `identityWithRuntimeDefault`: only one document can be the identity
and that one is the frozen 26.5 light patch, whose pin in tuned-profiles.test.ts
is the reason the default does not move.
It serves the two light standard profiles at both scales and the two light
accessibility profiles, exactly as the 26.5 light document does — the scale and
the accessibility state are axes of the capture and of the policy, not of the
material document.
Fitted on calibration and probe cells of apple-macos-27.0-1x-light-standard-glass0.5
at dpr 1 and checked on validation; the two constants that are inert at dpr 1 by
construction (rimWidth2x, sizeHeavyTapSigma2x) were fitted on the 2x profile.
W29 G3b (claims §5.154; Decision Log 6 (a)) refits the `outerShadow` block and
nothing else. The shadow is the one law G2 never read and G3 was therefore
forbidden to follow (§5.153 §5); it is read native-against-native in
`results/2026-09-19-w29-g3b-shadow-recede/` and the constants are fitted on the
departure the shadow axis measures. Every other key below is G3's, unchanged.
W30 G3 (claims §5.159; charter Decision Log 2 (b), 3 (c), 4 (b)) gives W30 G2's
eight inert operator leaves their values and refits the `outerShadow` block
jointly with them. The outer shadow's σ is now a function of the CASTING SPAN —
macOS 27 blurs it wider under a wider surface — and the six occlusion anchors
and `liftAmplitude` are refitted beside it, because their values carried the
compensation for the one σ this document shipped. Nothing outside the
`outerShadow` block and the scatter's five leaves moves.
W33 G1b, claims §5.172; Decision Log 1 (a), ruled: liftAmplitude is DECLARED 0,
not fitted. Apple's macOS 27 backdrop-black exterior is zero on 67 light / 50 dark
cells and 1,546,726 / 1,099,348 backdrop-black pixels (§5.170). The frozen macOS 26.5
material is nonzero on 39 of 125 cells and keeps its 0.01 / 0.0051 lifts and digests.
The three thick anchors take the rendered window-departure compensation (round B).
liftSpanMin and the lift's shape leaves stay, UNREAD at zero amplitude. The receded
difference already holds zero and is unchanged. No contour leaf or rim term moved
(W33 Decision Log 3, ruled); this is not a contour-stroke fit.
W36 G1, claims §5.179; Decision Log 5: the black branch alone.
Strength 1 carries the native span44 black ordinate, with thick explicitly equal to thin
as an unmeasured extrapolation. Support ends at encoded input 0.003, below the minimum
admitted packed impulse input 0.0031948897521942854. The middle and all old knots stay.
Both receded documents state their own black values over their active endpoint.
The separate receded colour-formula trial was declined at its frozen regression stops.

outerShadow.objective: shadow.meanDeparture{Native,Web}, linear light, over the whole exterior of the declared region

method: The band over which the material converges on its own backdrop, measured INERT
on macOS 27's light material and moved to the bottom of the range to say so.
On 26.5 the band ran 0.02 to 0.055 linear, so a surface over a near-black
backdrop adapted fully and vanished into it; that is why vitrea's capsule over
`dark-solid` rendered 0.0126 against a reference of 0.0126 and its capsule over
`impulse` rendered 0.0052.
On 27 the reference does not vanish anywhere on the bed: it reads 0.2899 over
`dark-solid` (encoded mean 0.110, linear 0.011) and 0.2389 over `impulse`
(encoded 0.004), at 5x and 45x their own backdrops. Claims §5.151 §4 found the
same thing from the other side — 55 of 66 cells whose silhouette collapses have
the collapse on 26.5, over `dark-solid`, `impulse`, `light-solid` and
`mid-dark-solid` — and the user's own eye named those cells on the W22 sheets.
So the constant that stood the response down over dark backdrops is the
constant that has to move, and the response below owns the level everywhere.
`backdropToneMax` is NOT the lever: the renderer multiplies it into the
response's own strength (`renderer.ts`, `toneStrength`), so zeroing it disables
the law being fitted. Measured: at max 0 every dark cell renders the bare
material at 0.4766 against a reference of 0.2899.
The law Decision Log 4 (a) ranks first, refit on the 27 bed. Four knots rather
than three, and the first at the bed's darkest backdrop rather than at its
darkest SOLID one: the solve's authority ramps from zero at half the first
anchor, so a first knot at 0.1104 left `impulse` ungoverned, which was right
while the reference vanished there and is wrong now.
Each ordinate is the reference's own settled level at that backdrop, corrected
once by the rendered residual — the solve lands the composite ON its target, so
one measured iteration closes it. Thin and thick are the reference's thin and
thick components at the same backdrop (capsule-button and rrect-sm against
rrect-md, -ml and -lg).
The finding inside the numbers: the two rows CONVERGE on 27. On 26.5 they
differ by 0.48 at the dark anchor (0.0126 against 0.4953) and on 27 by 0.024
(0.2835 against 0.3074) — the reference's level over a dark backdrop is now
very nearly independent of the surface's thickness, where it was the law's
largest split.
Residual, named rather than absorbed: over `mid-chroma-solid` the fitted curve
renders 0.61 against a reference of 0.385. That backdrop is chromatic and the
abscissa is a luminance, so the miss is the conditioning claims §5.151 §5 says
this bed cannot identify — not a knot that wants moving. It is a probe backdrop
and reaches no bound.
doesNotClose: The abscissa. §5.151 §5 refutes a constant and refutes the backdrop's mean
alone, and W28 §Deferred's identifying sitting is what would settle it.

method: Decision Log 4 (a) 2: two quantities moved, amplitude and width, and W23's fit
carries a constant for each.
Amplitude. The reference's radial rim peak fell by four to six times between the
beds on the same cells — `checkerboard__rrect-md__rest` 0.0904 to 0.0183,
`photo__rrect-md__rest` 0.0651 to 0.0146, `dark-solid__rrect-md__rest` 0.1233 to
0.0172 — while vitrea went on drawing the 26.5 amplitude. The pair is refitted
as the same affine law in the surface's own level: the peak is 0.336 of the
law's amplitude on every untinted cell whose body is under 0.9 (measured, five
backdrops), so the amplitude wanted is the reference's peak over that ratio, and
the least-squares line through the five backdrops is 0.115 − 0.122 x.
Width. The reference's rim FWHM rose from about 1.3 to about 2.2 CSS px on the
same cells, and `rim_weight` is (1 − |d|/width)², whose FWHM is 0.586 × width.
6.5 lands the rendered median exactly on the reference's.
`rimWidth2x` is fitted at dpr 2 and inert at dpr 1 by construction.
Decision Log 4 (a) 4: the diffusion moved as a function of the backdrop's
SPATIAL SCALE — fine structure survives 27 less and coarse structure more.
Read here as the interior's standard deviation per backdrop and as the
luminance transfer's slope, which order the backdrops the same way
independently (claims §5.151 §6).
A wider heavy component with a smaller sharp share is the direction that
suppresses the 16 px pitch while passing the photo: measured, σ 6 and 4.5 make
the checkerboard residual worse (+0.049 and +0.075 against +0.033) and σ 14 with
a 0.25 share brings the bed-wide signed mean of the transfer slope to 0.0000
doesNotClose: THE CAVEAT, and it is the largest residual this document carries. One kernel
cannot do what 27 does. At the fitted point the interior spread is +0.044 over
the reference passes LESS at one pitch and MORE at both the finer and the
coarser one, which a sharp-plus-heavy mix of two Gaussians cannot express at
once. The shape of the work that would close it is a scale-SELECTIVE scatter —
a second heavy tap at its own width, or a mix that is a function of the
backdrop's measured spatial scale rather than of the surface's span. It is not
added here: W28's mechanism precommit adds an operator when the delta shows a
structure the existing profile cannot fit, and this child's contract X3 limits
it to the smallest operator a NAMED structure needs; naming this one is what

method: Decision Log 4 (a) 6 says the tint's LIGHTNESS moved (ΔL median 0.026) and its
hue did not. Measured against the refitted material the twelve tinted light
cells read a ΔL residual of +0.0026 at the median and 0.0076 mean absolute —
inside the bed's own reading of the move. The tint's tone map therefore does
not move: the lightness change the native delta saw is carried by the body's
own level, which the response above refits, and moving the shade as well would
count it twice.
The CSS tier's half of the diffusion, derived from the same document in the same
wave. The dom tier has one `backdrop-filter` and no heavy tap, so the GPU
tier's kernel constants reach it only through the mix; measured, neither
`sizeScatterGainMax` nor the share moves its worst cell at all
(`checkerboard__rrect-ml__rest` 0.85817 against 0.85846 at gain 8 and 14).
This constant does: 1.6 takes that cell to 0.88808 and 2.2 to 0.90692, which
clears the adopted 0.90 — a row the 26.5 dom tier misses and holds by floor
(REGRESSION_FLOORS, 0.8748). The 27 dom tier meets it.

outerShadow.status: measured and fitted (W29 G3b, Decision Log 6 (a))
method: Apple's outer shadow moved on macOS 27 and G2 did not read it (claims §5.151
§2 lists the laws it read), so G3 was forbidden by X3 from following it and
recorded the finding instead (§5.153 §5). Decision Log 6 (a) ruled the read
and the refit. The read is native-against-native on the 27 bed at G2's own
bar, declared before the first 26.5 pair was opened
(`results/2026-09-19-w29-g3b-shadow-recede/bar-declaration.md`): the shadow
moved on EVERY measurable cell of every profile — 342 of 342 on the mean
departure, 246 of 246 on the fitted sigma and amplitude — at a median
delta/bar of 10^5 to 10^7.
sigmaPx 15.55 -> 11.0. The native sigma is no longer span-invariant (see
`sigmaIsNotSpanInvariantOn27` in fitted-shadow.json); 11.0 is the best single
value for the thick regime, where every row this refit exists to clear sits.
The amplitudes are solved from the departure. At sigma 11 with the 26.5
amplitudes the web reads 0.00648 / 0.01350 / 0.03052 on the checkerboard
capsule / rrect-md / rrect-ml against a 27 native of 0.00082 / 0.00379 /
0.01270, so the composited alpha each regime needs is the 26.5 alpha times
that ratio, and the occlusion follows by inverting sRGB's 2.4 power. Over the
three supported backdrops the thin regime wants 0.041-0.056, the 96 anchor
0.101-0.119 and the 128 anchor 0.192-0.209; the adopted numbers are those
means.
thickOcclusionAt160 is UNFITTED, as its 26.5 value was and for the same
reason: every span above 128 in the bed is holdout. 0.293 is the linear
extrapolation from the two fitted anchors, and the native corroborates the
shape rather than the value — its own falloff amplitude rises 0.1074 ->
0.1819 -> 0.2586 across spans 96 / 128 / 160, increments of 0.0745 and
0.0767, which is a straight line to 3 %.
liftAmplitude 0.01 -> 0.001, fitted on its own round. At 0 the bed-wide
signed departure residual is +0.00068 and at 0.004 it is -0.00186, so the
zero crossing is at 0.0011 and the lift is about a tenth of its 26.5 value.
The 27 shadow still adds light — it is not stood down — but far less of it.
reducedTransparencyOcclusion 0.197 -> 0.087, solved the same way on the
reduced-transparency profile's four identified active cells (checkerboard and
photo, capsule and rrect-md). **It is a compromise where 26.5's was a
measurement**: the 26.5 reference's exterior under the preference was flat at
0.192-0.202 thin and thick together, which is what justifies the fold writing
one amplitude into all six anchors. On 27 it is not flat — the native falloff
amplitude reads 0.165 at span 44, 0.111 at 96 and 0.251 at 160 — so the four
cells want 0.024 to 0.053 of alpha and 0.087 is their mean. Recorded as a
residual of the fold, not of the fit.
offsetPx, spreadPx, thinOcclusionDark, sizeGain, liftSpanMin, liftSpanFull
and liftBlurSigmaCss do NOT move, each for a reason. The offset is span-graded
on 27 like the sigma (4.0 CSS px at span 44, 7.5 at 96, 8.0 at 128) and 7.95
is already right where the rows are. thinOcclusionDark stays 0 because the
shadow is still analytically inert over black: the native reads 0.00000 over
`dark-solid` at span 44 and 0.00006 at span 96.
W30 G3 (claims §5.159) fits the σ law W30 G2 landed inert and refits the six
occlusion anchors and liftAmplitude jointly with it.
THE LAW. sigma_css(span) = sigmaPx + max(sigmaThinOffsetPx,
sigmaSlopePerSpan * (span - sigmaSpanRefPx)), evaluated per CASTER on both
tiers. sigmaSpanRefPx is HELD at 96 (Decision Log 3 (c)) because the law has a
flat direction — shifting sigmaPx, sigmaThinOffsetPx and sigmaSpanRefPx
together leaves sigma unchanged at every span — and sigmaPx is refitted as the
sigma at span 96, which is the span every bed carries sixteen cells at and the
span thickOcclusionAt96 is keyed to.
THE OBJECTIVE, and why it is not the departure. B1 is stated on the law's
closed form against each bed's median NATIVE sigma, so the law is solved from
W30 G0's cut before a candidate is rendered. Four objectives were computed
(results/2026-09-20-w30-g3-operators/shadow-law.txt) and the adopted one is the
point that maximises the smaller of B1's and B2's normalised slacks with the
slope held inside the range the served beds measure for themselves. An absolute
least squares lands the light document OUTSIDE B1's joint window, because a
squared absolute residual weights a span-160 observation four times a span-96
one and B1 is a relative clause; the window-constrained fit lands exactly on
the window's boundary.
THE FLOOR is a DECLARED reading and not a fit (Decision Log 2 (b)):
sigmaThinOffsetPx is sigmaSlopePerSpan * (44 - 96) exactly, which puts the
derived knee at span 44 and the floor at the thick line's own value there. The
thin cells are a position on the instrument's valley — the (amplitude, sigma)
pair trades at a constant product and the thin sigma bifurcates on the author's
TINT, which the material's blur cannot depend on.
THE ANCHORS are solved from the shadow axis's meanDeparture per regime,
anchor * (departure_native / departure_web), which is exact while the departure
is linear in the composited alpha at a fixed geometry. Three rounds; the
linearity holds to 2 % in every regime of both documents. thinOcclusionDark
stays exactly 0 (the native removes at most one or two of 255 codes over
dark-solid and impulse) and liftAmplitude does not move (the thick regimes
needed a scale, not a shape). thickOcclusionAt160 is FITTED here for the first
time, on the pitch ladder's ten span-160 rungs per standard bed — it was the
linear extrapolation from two anchors on 26.5 and on 27 until now.
WHAT DOES NOT MOVE, and what it costs. reducedTransparencyOcclusion is outside
contract X3 and stays at its W29 G3b value, so the reduced-transparency and
coupled-contrast beds' shadow moves through sigma alone. offsetPx stays at 7.95
and is the residual the thin regime's read sigma is now dominated by: the
native offset is span-graded like the sigma was — 3.0 to 4.5 CSS px at spans 32
and 44 against 7.5 to 8.0 at 96 and above — so at a thin caster vitrea's
exterior is dominated by a silhouette displaced about twice as far as Apple's.
That is the next span-graded length and §5.159 names it.
W30's scale-selective scatter (claims §5.156 §3, §5.158 §1, §5.159 §4), read
on the pitch ladder at a macOS 27 document for the first time — the reading W30
G0 could not have, because the macOS 27 generation of results/matrix.json
carried no probe row at all.
Five probe rounds. Candidate (i), the second heavy tap, is DECLINED on both
documents and candidate (ii), the scale gain about a reference, is adopted on
the dark document and declined on the light one. Both declines are
measurements:
- Candidate (i) cannot reach a pitch the FIRST heavy tap has already erased. A
second tap at 30 CSS px against the first's 14, at a share of 0.5, moves the
gated 16 px cell on 1x light by -0.0000. That is claims §5.158 §6's own trap,
reproduced on the bed it was predicted for.
- A second tap NARROWER than the first adds mid-band structure, which is the
wrong direction on the one bed in the whole capture that passes MORE
structure than Apple does: 1x light goes 1.5670 -> 1.8247 on that cell.
- Candidate (ii)'s statistic is SCALE-INVARIANT by construction. The analysis
reduction reads a fixed 64x64 grid off a mid-chain level, so one scene's edge
density is the same number at both scales — measured 0.170 at dpr 1 against
0.176 at dpr 2 on the dark bed's 16 px checkerboard. A per-source statistic
that cannot tell the scales apart cannot act in opposite directions on them,
which is what the light document's two beds need (1.567 and 0.425 on one
cell). At a gain of +2 the light document's 1x bed lands inside B4's window
and its 2x bed moves away from 1.0 by more; its two-bed ladder aggregate goes
The dark document takes -2 about 0.03, which moves both its beds toward 1.0 and
neither past it: the gated cell reads 0.7474 -> 0.9732 at 1x and 0.6367 ->
0.7665 at 2x. The reference is what keeps 1x below 1.0 — at a reference of 0
the same gain overshoots to 1.0222.
W31's chroma retention (claims §5.161 §5, fitted in §5.164 §4). How much of
the blurred backdrop's CHROMATICITY the body restores, at the luma the tone
solve produced. Fitted per SCHEME and per POSE: this document is the
light scheme's active endpoint and carries its own value, because the four
beds read 0.551 / 0.514 / 0.333 / 0.584 before the fit and are not one number.
Objective: R = chromaStructureRatioWeb / chromaStructureRatioNative, web
against native on the same cell and never against 1, median over the untinted
`photo` cells of the four macOS 27 standard profiles at both scales — 10 cells
on this bed — `calibration` + `validation`, WebGPU tier, holdout dropped by
construction in the fit loop's own reader. Bound 0.80 ≤ median R ≤ 1.20 with a
per-cell floor of 0.60, two-sided because an over-fitted retention adds chroma
the reference does not have.
Two rounds. Round A probed one point and measured the bed's slope; round B
solved it. R moves 0.5506 → 1.0486 on this bed, inside the bound and
inside the instrument's own 1x-against-2x reproducibility (4.5 % light, 9.1 %
dark), which is why there is no round C: a third would be fitting noise.
Both hard stops held with margin on every cell of the bed. The LEVEL stop —
|interiorMeanWeb − interiorMeanNative| ≤ 0.055, growing by no more than 0.005
from its pre-fit value — reads a worst |Δ| of 0.04932 and a worst growth of
+0.00006, eighty times inside the clause that binds, because the operator is
luma-preserving by construction. The STRUCTURE stop — interiorStdDevWeb within
2 % of its pre-fit value — reads a worst 1.317 %, on the bed's smallest
spread, and that residual is the capture's own 8-bit quantisation rather than
the operator: the movement scales inversely with the cell's spread.
The CSS tier carries NOTHING of this constant. A derived term was written,
rendered and declined on the measurement (§5.164 §5): on the dark bed it
bought nothing at all, and on the light bed it broke both stops.
